older.text: Flightcontrol – The AWS experience that didn't seem possible FlightControl FlightControl Home Documentation Pricing Blog Careers Company Log in Start free Build your dreams on AWS, effortlessly Flightcontrol is a PaaS that deploys to your AWS account Servers, Lambdas, workers, crons, static sites, databases & Redis We are your devops team with 24/7 emergency support Companies outgrowing other PaaS or homegrown AWS switch to Flightcontrol to regain reliability, security, and scalability at a reasonable cost Start free trial Get a demo Over $3 million of AWS resources under management The old way "Our AWS setup is consuming too much time & attention" Your team gets bogged down with complex Terraform scripts, manual configuration, and endless CI/CD pipelines. You could hire DevOps engineers, but they are expensive and it's hard to find really good ones. It will do the job, but now your developer productivity suffers as they are dependent on the infra team to make changes or spin up new services. The new way "Flightcontrol gives our team the power to manage bare metal AWS without needing to hire specific talent" Save thousands of dollars and months of time because Flightcontrol significantly reduces DevOps overhead. It empowers your developers ship like crazy without needing AWS or infrastructure expertise. Your developers gain full autonomy while benefiting from AWS's unmatched scalability, reliability, and flexibility. Simple, powerful deployments without worrying about low level AWS config We take the best AWS services , put together a best-in-class setup , and make them super easy to use . Connect your AWS account to Flightcontrol Connect your git repository to Flightcontrol Define your services (servers, APIs, databases, etc) Flightcontrol fully automates infrastructure provisioning, CI/CD, and deployments . All within your own AWS account where you retain full visibility and control Flightcontrol simplifies your deployments by providing a user-friendly dashboard designed specifically for developers , not DevOps engineers. Forget the frustration of navigating AWS’s overwhelming and fragmented console. With Flightcontrol, you see your entire infrastructure clearly in one intuitive interface, allowing you to manage deployments, services, and scaling with confidence. Deployments become as easy as a simple git push or webhook integration. Flightcontrol handles your CI/CD automation entirely, enabling your team to deploy confidently and quickly without maintaining complex Terraform or CDK scripts. You get the simplicity of platforms like Vercel or Heroku, paired with the raw power, near perfect reliability, and immense flexibility of AWS. Your developers can ship faster and stay focused on building great products. “Flightcontrol offers a nice balance between batteries-included and escape hatches that I haven't seen elsewhere. Keep up the good work and let us know if you need anything!” Matt Davis , Head of Technology | Spring Studios The Flightcontrol team allowed us to keep the seamless development experience of Vercel, but with the costs, control and flexibility of AWS. Not only their platform is great, the team went the extra mile to support us, no matter the day or time of day! Alfonso Gomez Jordana Manas , Founder | Crossmint We've been migrating our Rails app off of Heroku and onto AWS via Flightcontrol. The team is AWESOME and have built an excellent product. For our multiple locale deployments, 3-5 million monthly page views, use case, the Flightcontrol team were incredibly helpful in getting us setup + ensuring we understood what we had. 10/10 Tim Booker , COO | Lineup Publishing Without FlightControl it would simply not have been possible for our company to begin the migration process to AWS. They simplify so much of the AWS experience which allows primarily frontend developers such as myself to focus more on code and less on infrastructure. Infra devops cut down to zero! Deploying and scaling infra has been a dream. Preview environments mean no more conflicts on staging , no more delays, and significantly fewer bugs in production. Enable all stakeholders to see and test changes before merging code. Each preview environment is cost-optimized , intelligently sharing resources such as load balancers and RDS instances, ensuring you maintain control over spending. newer.text: Ravion: Agent-Native Cloud Infrastructure for AWS Ravion is the successor to Flightcontrol. Nothing changes for existing customers — your dashboard and docs are right where you left them. ✕ Use cases Docs Pricing Blog Careers Company Dashboard Log in Start free The agent-native cloud infrastructure platform for production-grade AWS Give developers and AI agents one governed way to provision, deploy, and operate applications in your AWS account. Move fast without building every DevOps capability yourself. Deploy this project with ravion.com/SKILL.md Trusted by engineering & platform teams at scale Your product needs AWS. Your team doesn’t have time to build the platform around it. You need more than your platform can give you Your deployment and reliability requirements no longer fit the platform’s fixed workflows. You don’t want to operate raw AWS yourself Getting infrastructure running is only the start. The team still has to assemble networking, permissions, pipelines, monitoring, and day-to-day operations. You can’t wait to build a DevOps team The engineers who could build that system are the same engineers needed on the product. Hiring takes time, and the roadmap cannot wait. With Ravion Start with the AWS system you would otherwise have to build. Provision, deploy, and operate through one connected system. AI Agent Step 1 Define what your application needs Start with Ravion’s production-ready modules, add your own modules, or connect existing Terraform. Developers and agents work through structured inputs instead of assembling the common path from scratch. Step 2 Review the plan before anything changes See exactly what Ravion will change, apply permissions and approval gates, and preserve an audit history of every action. Step 3 Build and deploy through one connected pipeline Run builds, approvals, deployments, and rollbacks through repeatable workflows with the complete deployment history attached. Step 4 See what happened. Recover without losing context Bring infrastructure changes, deployments, failures, and your existing logs and metrics together. Diagnose and recover through the UI, CLI, or API. We outgrew Heroku, but direct AWS was unrealistic. I love Ravion’s agent-friendly structure for getting great defaults on AWS while still being able to customize deployments just the way we need. And their support has been invaluable. Edgars Jekabsons, Engineering Manager / Ember { From static sites to multi-cloud infrastructure } Deploy web servers Ship containerized web services to ECS with rolling, blue-green, canary, or linear rollouts, or update EC2 hosts in place over SSM. Add shared load balancers, TLS certificates, and pre- or post-deploy hooks. Use it with AWS ECS AWS EC2 AWS ALB and many more Deploy to Kubernetes Coming soon Deploy background workers and AI agents Deploy Lambda functions Deploy static sites Provision databases and caches Provision networking, DNS, and certificates Deploy infrastructure across any cloud Loved by DevOps and Developers alike We switched from Railway for better reliability and avoiding AWS console. But Ravion’s expert support is what sold me. I’m always surprised by the speed and quality of responses. It’s a no brainer for startups that want to move fast. Yaser Alkayale, Co-founder / CivCore Frequently asked questions How is Ravion different from Terraform Cloud or Spacelift? Ravion does everything you'd expect from a Terraform automation platform: remote plans and applies, managed state, versioned resource history, drift detection, approval gates, and policy checks. The difference is that modules are the product. Each module also carries its builds, deploys, rollbacks, logs, and metrics, so developers get a self-service interface instead of a pile of HCL and a run queue. Learn about stacks How is Ravion different from a PaaS? A PaaS hosts your app on their infrastructure, and you're capped by whatever they choose to expose. Ravion provisions everything in your own AWS account, so you get dedicated infrastructure, direct cloud pricing, easier compliance, and no wall to hit as you scale. The developer experience feels like a PaaS. The ceiling is the entire cloud, and there's no painful migration waiting for you later. Read our product philosophy Do I have to write Terraform? No. Most teams start with our standard library of production-ready modules, including VPCs, ECS and EC2 services, RDS, Aurora, ElastiCache, Lambda, and static sites, configured through typed inputs in the dashboard or a YAML file. When you need something custom, bring your own Terraform: run it through Ravion directly, or package it into a reusable module with typed inputs your team can self-serve. Explore the standard library Can I use CloudFormation, Pulumi, or CDK? Not today. Pipelines run Terraform and OpenTofu, so CloudFormation, AWS CDK, Pulumi, CDK for Terraform, SST, and the Serverless Framework aren't supported yet, though support for more IaC tools is planned. If you have infrastructure in one of those tools already, you don't have to rewrite it to get started: import the existing resources into a Ravion module's Terraform state and leave the rest where it is. Read the import guide Which clouds does Ravion support? Our standard library modules and pipeline runners are AWS today. Runners are temporary EC2 instances in your own account, and the native modules cover the common AWS building blocks. That doesn't limit you to AWS: authenticate a runner with credentials for any other provider, passed in as environment variables from Secrets Manager or Parameter Store, and you can manage GCP, Azure, Cloudflare, Datadog, or anything else Terraform supports, with the same plans, approvals, and state history. See the Terraform stack module Is support for GCP and Azure coming? Yes. Native GCP and Azure modules and pipeline runners are coming. Until then, you can provision both clouds today by authenticating an AWS pipeline runner with the appropriate provider credentials and running your Terraform or OpenTofu through Ravion. Is there vendor lock-in? No. Ravion runs open source Terraform and OpenTofu in your own cloud account, and our standard library modules are open source too. Fork them, lock them down, or replace them entirely with your own. Your projects, environments, modules, and pipelines are config as code you can pull down as plain YAML at any time, and Terraform state lives in your own S3 backend or in our managed backend, which you can also pull whenever you want. View the open source modules What happens if Ravion goes away? Your infrastructure keeps running, because it was never ours. Every resource lives in your cloud account, provisioned by open source Terraform, using state you can pull with one command. Worst case, you keep the state and the modules and run plans and applies yourself, exactly as if you'd always managed them by hand. You'd lose our dashboard and pipelines, not your infrastructure. Read about state storage What happens if Ravion has downtime? Your apps stay up. No requests, traffic, or customer data pass through Ravion. It's a control plane that automates your cloud account, so an outage on our side never touches your running services, databases, or load balancers. New builds, deploys, and Terraform runs wait until we're back, and your cloud provider's console and CLI are always there as an escape hatch. See how Ravion works What access does Ravion need to my AWS account? You connect an account by creating an IAM role with a CloudFormation stack we walk you through, and deleting that stack permanently revokes our access. Terraform, builds, and pipelines execute on temporary EC2 instances inside your own account, so your source code never enters our control plane and runtime secrets stay in AWS Secrets Manager or Parameter Store. Read about security Can I bring infrastructure I already have? Yes. Existing resources can be imported into a Ravion module's Terraform state without recreating or destroying anything, whether you're importing into a standard library module or into your own Terraform. Coming from Flightcontrol, there's a guided migration you can run service by service, since both products share the same organization and can run side by side. Read the import guide Is Ravion safe for AI agents to use? It's a design goal. Agents work through the CLI, API, and MCP server against config as code: dry run first, review the diff, then apply. Every infrastructure change runs through a pipeline with a visible Terraform plan and an approval gate you control, and agents pick from the modules your platform team approved instead of hand-writing IaC. They get speed inside boundaries you set. Start here with an agent How old is the company? Our company was founded in 2021 and brought Flightcontrol to profitability. Development on Ravion began in June 2025, and Ravion has had production users since spring 2026. Visit Flightcontrol What does Ravion cost? Ravion is free for individuals, with 1 user, up to 50 modules, and 2,000 pipeline minutes. Team is pay as you go with no platform fee and no seat pricing: modules are free, $5, or $30 per month depending on category, and 50,000 pipeline minutes are included. You always pay your cloud provider directly for the underlying infrastructure, with no markup from us. See pricing Provision and deploy your first app in minutes Connect your AWS account, pick a module, and ship. An execution is a single durable function run plus each step inside it. If your function has 5 step.run() calls, one run uses 6 executions (the run itself + 5 steps). What happens if I exceed the included executions on my plan? Pro plans bill metered usage above the included executions at tiered rates — the more you use, the lower the per-execution price. Hobby plans pause execution once the free quota is exhausted; upgrade to keep running. Can I switch plans later? Yes. Plan changes take effect immediately and prorate the current billing cycle. Can I self-host Inngest? Yes. Inngest is open-source and can be self-hosted. Turnaround times depend on your plan and can be as low as 2 days for Enterprise customers. What are Connections, Function compute time, and Data Transfer? 1 Connection = 1 API key or access token of the external API. For example: 3 users connect their Gmail = 3 connections. Connections are pro-rated for the time they are stored in your account. Function compute time measures how long your integrations run. Each run is rounded up to the nearest second. For example, if a tool call takes 300ms, you will be billed for 1 second of Function compute time. A sync that runs once an hour and takes 3 seconds per run consumes 24 x 3 = 72 seconds of compute time per day. Tool calls, syncs, and actions consume function compute time. Data Transfer measures the amount of data Nango processes for your integrations. This includes: Data sent from Nango to your backend Data sent from Nango to external APIs Data processed by Nango’s syncs Custom log messages you emit from your Nango Functions We only measure egress. Ingress transfers are free. Do you offer volume discounts? We offer significant volume discounts, with commitments, across all pricing metrics on the Enterprise plan. For example, connections can be as low as $0.01/connection/month at scale. Please reach out with your expected volumes for a custom quote! Is Nango suitable for high-volume use cases? Yes, definitely. We serve B2C and Fortune 500 companies. Our platform is built for high throughput, and all components scale horizontally. Compare every plan side by side FAQs Frequently asked questions. Can I use microlink for free? Absolutely. We have a forever free endpoint you can use. It’s the best way to start using the service. The free plan runs under some limitations to avoid abusive usage of the platform, like burst rate, limited concurrency rate and daily rate limit. The free plan should be enough for small projects or low API quota. How different is the free plan compared with the Pro plan? The pro plan is ready to be used at scale, with better performance and unlocked features such as headers , ttl or proxy . A Pro plan comes with an associated API key and configurable quota. You only pay as you need. What if I don't know how much API quota I need? No problem, just start with the smallest pro plan, and at the moment you need more, you can upgrade your plan. How do I get an API key? After your payment, we send you the API key associated with the email you signed up. The API key needs to be attached to all your requests: In Microlink SDK , attach it as apiKey . In Microlink API , attach it as a header . What's your SLA level? Our Service-Level Agreements commitment is 99.9% (three nines). You can see the live status of the service. How do I know my plan usage? We notify you automatically when you reach 80% or more of your usage plan, offering to upgrade your plan to one more suitable based on your plan usage. What if I want to change my plan? You can upgrade, downgrade, or cancel your monthly account at any time with no further obligation by sending an email to [email protected] with the email you signed up. How is the payment processed? We use Stripe to process your payment. It’s the same payment provider used in products such as Twitter, Pinterest, and Lyft. We do not handle your credit card information directly. Can I update my card details? Yes, send an email to [email protected] requesting the change. You will receive a link where you'll be able to securely update your details. Can I cancel my subscription? Yes, by sending an email to [email protected] . Your request will be processed within 24hrs. Other questions? We’re always available at [email protected] . Install the Chrome extension, record your flow directly in the browser, and turn it into an automated end-to-end test without setting up a complex framework. You can run tests locally, schedule them in the cloud, and use AI-assisted recording to reduce flaky steps and maintenance. Do I need deep technical skills to use BugBug? BugBug is designed for both - less technical and technical users, like QA engineers, testers, developers, and SaaS teams who want to automate testing without relying heavily on writing code. It’s perfect for teams with mixed skill sets - especially helpful for small and mid-sized teams that need reliable test coverage but don’t want the overhead of a large QA department. Less technical users can record and maintain tests visually, while technical users can extend tests with JavaScript, API/CLI access, CI/CD integrations, variables, and conditions. Custom JavaScript actions – add your own JavaScript steps and assertions. Reusable components – avoid unnecessary repetition when creating tests. Variables and conditions – add logic to your test scenarios. CI/CD integration – run tests automatically via GitHub Actions, Jenkins, or CLI. Advanced reporting - download compliance-ready reports with screenshots and export test data in formats like JSON or CSV. See all features Can I run BugBug tests in CI/CD pipelines? Yes, you can integrate BugBug with your CI/CD build pipelines, such as Github, Gitlab, Travis, Jenkins, or Bitbucket, via Command Line Interface (CLI) or BugBug's public API. Does BugBug support parallel test execution? Yes, BugBug supports running tests in parallel, so you can execute multiple tests at the same time instead of waiting for them to run one-by-one. This is especially useful for CI/CD pipelines where you want fast feedback on every pull request or deployment. Read more about parallel execution here. Start testing. It's free 4.7 / 5 Trusted by SaaS companies in 50+ countries Testing for AI-speed releases BugBug helps teams stay ahead of regression testing as code ships faster than QA can keep up. Coverage Scale coverage, not QA team AI-speed releases create more critical flows than small QA teams can realistically test before every release. With BugBug Turn new flows into tests in minutes Run regression checks before release Test more with the same team Catch AI-code bugs early Efficiency Free frameworks still cost time Playwright and Cypress are free, but setup, infrastructure, and maintenance still cost developer time. With BugBug No test framework setup No XPath or selector maintenance Less developer time spent fixing tests QA can maintain tests without dev support From manual check to automated regression in 3 steps Build coverage around your most important user flows in one afternoon. Record critical flows Use BugBug AI Test Recorder to capture user flows directly in your browser. Edit and maintain faster User-friendly interface allow you to fix and update tests with ease. Run before every release Schedule cloud runs before every release. Get notifications when tests fail. " BugBug cut manual regression testing, freeing us to focus on other critical tasks. Reuse steps, debug failures faster, and give stakeholders clear visibility into test results. Compare plans Fast setup & simplicity Empower cross-functional teams Fully codeless, AI test recorder The easiest tool out there No framework setup Unlimited testing Expand test coverage without limits Unlimited local & cloud runs Unlimited users Unlimited built-in email testing Predictable cost Scale freely with a fixed price Free plan with unlimited tests No seat-based pricing No infrastructure to mantain Compare plans Your next release. Properly tested. Join 1,200+ QA teams that automated their regression coverage with BugBug. Start testing. It's free. Free plan No credit card 14-days trial Ready to catch some bugs? Need more time to think? Click below to shoot some bugs while you digest why BugBug is the best low-code testing tool. Start testing. It's free Frequently Asked Questions Why is BugBug the easiest test automation tool? BugBug is built to make test automation easy from the first test. Install the Chrome extension, record your flow directly in the browser, and turn it into an automated end-to-end test without setting up a complex framework. You can run tests locally, schedule them in the cloud, and use AI-assisted recording to reduce flaky steps and maintenance. Do I need deep technical skills to use BugBug? BugBug is designed for both - less technical and technical users, like QA engineers, testers, developers, and SaaS teams who want to automate testing without relying heavily on writing code. It’s perfect for teams with mixed skill sets - especially helpful for small and mid-sized teams that need reliable test coverage but don’t want the overhead of a large QA department. See the beginners' tutorial Is BugBug right for a small QA team? Yes. BugBug is built for teams of 1–5 QA engineers who need broad coverage without deep engineering support. Is BugBug only for non-technical users? No. QA engineers, developers, and product teams can all use BugBug. Less technical users can record and maintain tests visually, while technical users can extend tests with JavaScript, API/CLI access, CI/CD integrations, variables, and conditions. Can I import and export my BugBug tests? Yes. Export individual tests as human-readable YAML for review, editing, and version control. For a complete backup, including components and required files, export your test or project as a ZIP. Your test assets aren’t locked inside BugBug. How does BugBug reduce flaky tests? BugBug uses adaptive locators, smart waiting, and smart click-and-scroll behavior to make recorded tests more stable on dynamic web applications. What makes BugBug different? BugBug is a lightweight test automation tool built for simplicity—no complex setup, coding, or costly onboarding required. It’s fast, easy to use, and affordable. Here’s how BugBug stands out: Robust selectors recording – Record tests simply by clicking in your browser. Truly user-friendly interface – Intuitive UI makes testing effortless. Unlimited local and cloud runs – Test as much as you want, without limits. No vendor lock-in – Import and export tests as human-readable YAML files for backup, review, version control. Cloud runs on schedule – Schedule cloud testing with daily health checks. CI/CD integration – Plug BugBug into your pipeline in minutes. Unlimited users – Invite as many team members as you like. See all features Which types of software testing can I do with BugBug? BugBug is perfect for testing web applications and websites built on Chromium-based browsers. You can perform: End-to-end (E2E) testing to validate user flows. Regression testing to catch breaking changes. Smoke testing to verify critical paths. UI testing to verify user interactions. See our test automation guides Which browsers does BugBug support? BugBug supports all Chromium-based browsers, like Google Chrome, Edge, Opera, Brave, etc. Do you offer unlimited users/seats? Yes, on Pro and Business every team member is included at no extra cost, with no per-seat pricing, ever. Free comes with 1 user and Core with 3, so you can get started and prove out your first regression suite before scaling. Once you move to Pro, seats stop being a variable: unlimited users, unlimited projects, unlimited tests, one flat price. What advanced features does BugBug offer? BugBug includes many advanced features that help teams scale their testing efforts: Cloud scheduling – run tests daily or after every deployment. BugBug Inbox Testing – verify and test your user signup or login process without a hassle while recording your test. Edit & Rewind – jump back in your test scenario without starting over. Custom JavaScript actions – add your own JavaScript steps and assertions. Reusable components – avoid unnecessary repetition when creating tests. Variables and conditions – add logic to your test scenarios. CI/CD integration – run tests automatically via GitHub Actions, Jenkins, or CLI. Advanced reporting - download compliance-ready reports with screenshots and export test data in formats like JSON or CSV. See all features Can I run BugBug tests in CI/CD pipelines? Yes, you can integrate BugBug with your CI/CD build pipelines, such as Github, Gitlab, Travis, Jenkins, or Bitbucket, via Command Line Interface (CLI) or BugBug's public API. Does BugBug support parallel test execution? Yes, BugBug supports running tests in parallel, so you can execute multiple tests at the same time instead of waiting for them to run one-by-one. This is especially useful for CI/CD pipelines where you want fast feedback on every pull request or deployment. Read more about parallel execution here. We already have Cypress/Playwright tests — can BugBug work alongside them? Yes. BugBug runs independently and integrates into the same CI/CD pipeline. Many teams use BugBug for their critical path regression and maintain Playwright for unit-adjacent tests. When is BugBug not the right fit? BugBug is focused on Chromium-based web apps and websites. It is not a native mobile, desktop, Safari, or Firefox automation platform. Is BugBug a replacement for QA engineers? No. BugBug helps QA teams automate repetitive regression checks, expand coverage, and spend more time on exploratory testing, edge cases, and release quality. Can I use BugBug for free? Yes! BugBug offers the Free Plan with: Unlimited local test runs 15 tests 4 test suites 1 user 1 project AI Test recorder Components Edit & rewind Screenshots 7 days of tests history If you need cloud features like test scheduling, CI/CD integration, or running tests on multiple environments, you can upgrade to one of the paid plans. Check pricing Do you offer startup discounts? Who qualifies? Yes, BugBug offers a startup discount for eligible early-stage companies. Learn more about the Startup Discount Program. Where is customer data hosted (EU/US)? BugBug’s primary infrastructure is hosted in the EU specifically, BugBug's servers are located in Gdańsk, Poland. More questions bugging you? Get a demo We use cookies on our website to give you the most relevant experience by remembering your preferences. By clicking “Accept”, you consent to the use of all the cookies. LangSmith Observability & Evaluation Questions What is a trace? Can it contain multiple events? A trace represents a single execution of your application—whether it’s an agent, evaluator, or playground session. It can include many individual steps, such as LLM calls and other tracked events. Here's an example of a single trace. What is the difference between a base trace and an extended trace? Base traces have a shorter retention period of 14 days and cost $2.50 per 1k traces. Extended traces have a longer retention period of 400 days and cost $5.00 per 1k traces. You can "upgrade" base traces to extended traces at $2.50 per 1k traces. Why would I upgrade a base trace to an extended trace? Base traces are short-lived (14-day retention) and ideal for quick debugging or ad-hoc analysis. They’re priced for volume and short-term utility. Extended traces, on the other hand, are retained for 400 days and often include valuable feedback—whether from users, evaluators, or human labelers. This feedback makes them essential for ongoing improvement and model tuning (higher utility), which comes with a higher price point. LangSmith lets you choose the right retention for each trace, helping you balance cost and value. LangSmith Deployment Questions Does LangSmith Deployment include any free deployments? Plus plans include 1 free dev-sized deployment. If you spin up additional dev-sized or production-sized deployments, you’ll be charged by usage (deployment runs and uptime). For my free Dev agent deployment for LangSmith Deployment, is there a cap on the number of deployment runs? If you’re on the Plus plan, you get 1 free dev-sized agent deployment – all usage in this deployment will be free no matter how many deployment runs you execute. How do you define deployment runs? A deployment run is one end-to-end invocation of a LangGraph agent deployed via LangSmith Deployment. Nodes and subgraphs within a single agent execution are not charged separately. Calls to other LangGraph agents (through RemoteGraph or the LangGraph SDK or the API directly) are charged separately, to the deployment that hosts the agent being called. An interrupt for human-in-the-loop creates a separate deployment run when resuming. For Plus plans, Deployment Runs are billed at $0.005 each. Enterprise pricing is customized based on customer requirements, including support needs. What does uptime mean for LangSmith Deployment usage? Uptime is the duration your deployment’s database is live and persisting state. Uptime will be tracked as soon as your deployment is live and ends when you shut it down. Dev agent deployments are typically short-lived (used during iteration, then deleted) – whereas Production agent deployments stay live and are updated via revisions (rather than being deleted). When should I use a dev-sized deployment vs. a production-sized agent deployment? We recommend using the production-sized deployment for any customer-facing agent. Dev-sized agent deployments are intended for testing and do not support horizontal scaling, backups, or performance optimizations needed in production. LangSmith Fleet Questions What is a Fleet run? A Fleet run is a single execution (a complete invocation) of an agent. Runs occur when you create, test, or run an agent. A Fleet run includes any message delivered to the agent through configured triggers (including third-party integrations or other connected services) as well as messages sent directly through the Fleet user interface (e.g., via the chat interface). An interrupt for human-in-the-loop creates a separate Fleet run when resuming. An execution failure does not count as a Fleet run. Are model costs included with Fleet pricing? No. Model usage is billed separately by your model provider. Fleet lets you choose the model you want (for example, Anthropic, OpenAI, Gemini, or another provider) and connect it using your provider API key. More information on configuring models in our docs . Are agent tools included with Fleet pricing? Fleet includes built-in tools and supports connecting third-party tools via a remote MCP server. Third-party tools typically require you to authenticate with your account, and any fees or usage charges are billed by the third-party provider. More information on setting up tool keys in our docs . Are Fleet runs automatically traced in LangSmith, and do they count toward billing? Yes. Every Fleet run is automatically traced in LangSmith. These traces are attributed to the user’s account and count toward usage-based billing under the customer’s LangSmith plan. Can I self-host Fleet? Self-hosting for Fleet is currently available in Beta. Contact our sales team to learn more. How do I disable Fleet? If you are on a self-hosted LangSmith instance, you can disable Fleet by setting the following to false in your values.yaml : backend: agentBootstrap: enabled: false config: agentBuilder: enabled: false agentBuilderToolServer: enabled: false agentBuilderTriggerServer: enabled: false If you are on cloud LangSmith, reach out to our Support team to disable Fleet. ‍ LangSmith Engine Questions How is LangSmith Engine priced? Engine is metered in LCUs (LangChain Compute Units), which are consumed during each Engine run. 1 LCU costs $1.50. What does a LangChain Compute Unit (LCU) represent? An LCU represents a unit of work done by Engine. This includes the compute, infrastructure, and underlying model usage needed to analyze traces, identify issues, and propose fixes to your agent. How are LCUs calculated? Typical usage depends on whether Engine is running for the first time or on its regular schedule: Initial run: about 30 to 40 LCUs Recurring runs: about 10 to 15 LCUs every 6 hours These ranges are estimates. Actual usage depends on the amount of work Engine performs, including the volume of traces analyzed, the number of issues surfaced, the number of proposed fixes generated, and the complexity of your application. How often does Engine run? Engine is scheduled to run once every 6 hours. Is model usage included in the cost? Yes. Engine pricing includes the underlying model usage required for analysis and fix generation. Where can I see my LCU usage? You can view your organization’s LCU usage in your LangSmith billing console by visiting Settings > Billing. Learn more . Are LCUs included in my plan? Plus plans: LCUs are an additional charge on top of your monthly license fee and any other product usage. Enterprise plans: LCUs are charged against your committed LangChain credits. How do I disable Engine? Ask your Organization Admin to turn off Engine in the Settings page by following instructions here . Once Engine is disabled, it will stop running on its regular schedule and will no longer consume LCUs. LangSmith Sandboxes Questions How is Sandbox uptime calculated? Sandboxes are designed as ephemeral compute environments and are billed per second. LangSmith Sandboxes have configurable TTLs so inactive sandboxes shut down automatically. Are Langsmith Sandboxes available for self hosted deployments? Not currently. Sandboxes are available for SaaS Cloud deployments. Ready to start shipping reliable agents faster? Powerful API, hosting, integrations and developer tools Unmatched customer support Start for free No credit card required ∙ 5-minute setup " The product and support are fantastic . " Laars Buur | CTO " The support is blazing fast , thank you Jakub! " Stefan | Developer " Interface that makes any dev feel at home ! " Dario De Cianni | CTO " Excellent app, saves my time and money " Dmitry Melnik | Developer Frequently asked questions What are translation keys? One translation key can be translated into many language translations. Such approach makes your costs more predictable. Do not confuse it with a 'translation' or 'string'. Learn more about translation keys . How do I get a VAT refund? Fill your VAT number during the checkout process, and if you are eligible, VAT will be deducted from your invoice. If you did not add it during the checkout, you can add it later on on the invoice page. See how to add a VAT number . What are auto-translation characters? Auto-translation character is a character that is sent from your source translation to external service like Google Translate to translate it to another language. For example, translating "Hello World" (11 characters including space) to 5 languages will consume 55 characters (11 characters x 5 languages). Do auto-translate characters rollover? Yes, unused auto-translation characters rollover to the following months and they are valid until your subscription plan is active. You can gather up to 2 million unused characters in your account. Can I use your own API keys for auto-translation? Yes, you can use your own API keys for auto-translation services. Using your own API key doesn't consume auto-translation characters from your SimpleLocalize plan. Can I change plan limits? Yes, you can switch between plans at any time. You can also change your current plan limits, such as the number of translation keys, adding more auto-translation characters, or adding more users. The price will be adjusted accordingly based on the remaining time in your billing cycle. What are per-customer translations? Per-customer translations allow you to create custom translations for each of your customers. This is useful when you want to provide personalized content or translations for specific users. Learn more about per-customer translations . Do you offer custom plans? Yes, we offer custom plans for large teams and enterprises. Contact us at contact@simplelocalize.io to learn more. terms_then: Startup scholarship Get one year of free access to the Amplitude Growth plan—including Analytics, Feature and Web Experimentation, Session Replay, and Activation—plus competitive discounts for life. Criteria: Less than $10M in funding raised Fewer than 20 employees
The Amplitude Growth plan has a data limit of 200,000 monthly tracked users (MTUs).
You can also choose to measure data use by event volume (100M events/month) instead of MTUs if it helps extend your data usage.

You won’t be charged if you exceed the 200K MTUs included with the Growth plan each month. Instead, we’ll contact you about lowering your MTU count the following month. You can always upgrade to get more MTUs. If you exceed the MTU count more than twice, you’ll be downgraded to our free Starter plan.

terms_on_record_day: Early Stage Startup Pricing Your first year of Amplitude is 100% free Everything: product analytics, session replays, MCP, and agents. Up to 100M events a month. $60,000 value. Year two, 40% off.
Year 1 100% off The full Growth plan. Every feature, unlimited teammates, no credit card.
Or stay free, for good Drop to the free 2M-events/month plan and keep your data and dashboards. No penalty.
What are the limits? 200K monthly tracked users or 100M events/month - for a typical B2B SaaS that's roughly 6,000 monthly active users, usually plenty for early-stage teams.
Sixty days before it ends we send a usage-based quote for year two, and you keep a standing startup discount off list price after that.
Startup alumni keep discounts on Plus and Growth annual plans.

An MTU is a unique user who triggers one or more events in an analytics or experimentation project in a calendar month. This can be either an anonymous user (which Amplitude tracks via device ID) or an identified user (tracked by user ID). Basically, the more user interactions tracked across all projects in a month, the higher the MTU count. Other models, including all image and speech-to-text models, need Pro ($12/mo) or a paid balance.
